scope: Theorem 1.1 (Prescribed-order signed prefixes) of the manuscript “The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström theorem” (preprints/The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem-September-24-2026/The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 097 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d8924ac01b6d4dc0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant C such that, for all integers d, N ≥ 1 and every sequence v1, . . . , vN ∈ Rd with ∥vi∥2 ≤ 1, there are signs ε1, . . . , εN ∈ {−1, 1} for which max 0≤k≤N ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ k ∑ i=1 εivi ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ 2 ≤ C √ d. The same signs control all prefixes, and C is independent of d, N and the sequence.
